title: Writing it down
hook: write what you've learned for those after you
tomorrow: a nine-year-old says thank you. who should Amira thank?

segments.voice: Yesterday, welcoming questions: they're how people come to know one another. Some of the best answers sit with the oldest person in the family.

A grandmother on speakerphone, telling the story of her own mother's prayer beads, the third time this year. Somebody says, I'll remember this one. Nobody quite does. A phone can hold years of photos and not one minute of how she tells it. So how do you keep what an elder knows? The Qur'an names the tool right in its text: the pen.
screen: `A STORY ON SPEAKERPHONE.` → `I'LL REMEMBER. NOBODY DOES.` → `THE PEN.`

segments.voice: In Pickthall's words, God is the one "Who teacheth by the pen, Teacheth man that which he knew not." Another surah opens with an oath on the pen itself: "Nun. By the pen and that which they write (therein)." And when the Qur'an turns to lending money, it starts with paperwork: "O ye who believe! When ye contract a debt for a fixed term, record it in writing." Writing protects people from their own memory. A report in Sunan Abu Dawud tells of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who wrote down what he heard the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say. Some people warned him off: he's human, they said, he speaks when he's angry and when he's pleased. So 'Abdullah stopped and asked. The Prophet pointed to his own mouth and told him to write, because nothing came from it but truth. Now the senses. Writing by hand is slow on purpose. The scratch of the pen. The drag of ink. The weight of a page your hand had to fill. A hand that's writing can't skim, so it keeps what a quick glance would lose. And a page, unlike a memory, can be handed to someone younger. One to tell a friend tonight: the Qur'an swears an oath by the pen and that which they write.
screen: `TAUGHT BY THE PEN.` · `RECORD IT IN WRITING.` · `'WRITE': NOTHING BUT TRUTH.` · `A HAND CAN'T SKIM.` · then, large: `WRITE IT DOWN.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and any scrap of paper. Write one thing someone older taught you, in their words if you can, with their name underneath. Go slowly enough to hear the pen move, and keep the page.
screen: `A PEN, A SCRAP OF PAPER.` · `THEIR WORDS, THEIR NAME.` · `HEAR THE PEN.`

segments.voice: Writing it down: keeping what you've learned on paper for whoever comes after you. The Qur'an swears by the pen.
Pocket this: write it down, because a page waits when memory won't. Eight of ten, in ink.

fork.setup: your study group has one member who 'just remembers' everything and won't add to the shared notes. the exam is in a week, and she's sick for two days. what fits today?

write the notes down together now, so nobody depends on one head.
wait until she's back. she'll fill everyone in afterward.
fork.reveal: 2:282 asks for writing so no one relies on memory alone. a page can be handed on; a head can get sick.

Just listen closely. If it matters, you'll remember it word for word.

chat.meaning: The Qur'an names the pen as how God teaches and asks for important things in writing. Memory slips; a page waits for whoever comes next.
